arxiv-1604-08706.title: Comment on Quantum Massive Conformal Gravity
arxiv-1604-08706.description: Abstract In a recent paper in EPJC March 2016, Faria has shown that quantum massive conformal gravity is renormalizable but has ghost states. We comment this paper on the aspect of renormalizability. Yun Soo Myung * * * e-mail address: ysmyung@inje.ac.

arxiv-2102-03794.title: A self-adaptive and robust fission clustering algorithm via heat diffusion and maximal turning angle
arxiv-2102-03794.creator: Yu Han 1 , Shizhan Lu 2 , Haiyan Xu 1∗
arxiv-2102-03794.description: Abstract Cluster analysis, which focuses on the grouping and categorization of similar elements, is widely used in various fields of research. A novel and fast clustering algorithm, fission clustering algorithm, is proposed in recent year. In this article, we propose a robust fission clustering (RFC) algorithm and a self-adaptive noise identification method.

arxiv-2211-09643.title: CPT-V: A Contrastive Approach to Post-Training Quantization of Vision Transformers
arxiv-2211-09643.creator: Natalia Frumkin, Dibakar Gope, Diana Marculescu
arxiv-2211-09643.description: Abstract When considering post-training quantization, prior work has typically focused on developing a mixed precision scheme or learning the best way to partition a network for quantization. In our work, CPT-V, we look at a general way to improve the accuracy of networks that have already been quantized, simply by perturbing the quantization scales.

arxiv-2308-00306.title: Smoothed Analysis of the 2-Opt Heuristic for the TSP under Gaussian Noise Thanks: This paper is based on results presented at ISAAC 2013 [ 22 ] and ICALP 2015 [ 19 ] .
arxiv-2308-00306.creator: Marvin Künnemann, Bodo Manthey, Rianne Veenstra
arxiv-2308-00306.description: Abstract The 2-opt heuristic is a very simple local search heuristic for the traveling salesperson problem. In practice it usually converges quickly to solutions within a few percentages of optimality. In contrast to this, its running-time is exponential and its approximation performance is poor in the worst case.

arxiv-2310-14384.title: ARCOQ: Arabic Closest Opposite Questions Dataset
arxiv-2310-14384.creator: Sandra Rizkallah, Amir F. Atiya, Samir Shaheen
arxiv-2310-14384.description: Abstract This paper presents a dataset for closest opposite questions in Arabic language. The dataset is the first of its kind for the Arabic language. It is beneficial for the assessment of systems on the aspect of antonymy detection. The structure is similar to that of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) closest opposite questions dataset for the English language.

arxiv-2508-18972.title: Amplifying Two-Mode Squeezing in Nanomechanical Resonators
arxiv-2508-18972.creator: Muhdin Abdo Wodedo, Tesfay Gebremariam Tesfahannes, Tewodros Yirgashewa Darge, Mauro Pereira, Berihu Teklu
arxiv-2508-18972.description: Abstract Quantum squeezing plays a crucial role in enhancing the precision of quantum metrology and improving the efficiency of quantum information processing protocols. We thus propose a scheme to amplify two-mode squeezing in nanomechanical resonators, harnessing parametric amplification and two-tone laser controls.

arxiv-2510-12555.title: Inclusive Fitness as a Key Step Towards More Advanced Social Behaviors in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Settings Conference: ; ;
arxiv-2510-12555.creator: Andries Rosseau, Raphaël Avalos, Ann Nowé
arxiv-2510-12555.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andries Rosseau, Raphaël Avalos, Ann Nowé. The competitive and cooperative forces of natural selection have driven the evolution of intelligence for millions of years, culminating in nature’s vast biodiversity and the complexity of human minds. Inspired by this process, we propose a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning framework where each agent is assigned a genotype and where reward functions are modelled after the concept of inclusive fitness.

arxiv-2512-22705.title: GHaLIB: A Multilingual Framework for Hope Speech Detection in Low-Resource Languages
arxiv-2512-22705.creator: Ahmed Abdullah, Haroon Mahmood, Sana Fatima
arxiv-2512-22705.description: Abstract Hope speech has been relatively underrepresented in Natural Language Processing (NLP). Current studies are largely focused on English, which has resulted in a lack of resources for low-resource languages such as Urdu. As a result, the creation of tools that facilitate positive online communication remains limited.

arxiv-2602-23764.title: A new class of coherent states involving Fox-Wright functions and their generalization in the bicomplex framework Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author
arxiv-2602-23764.creator: Snehasis Bera, Sourav Das, Abhijit Banerjee ∗
arxiv-2602-23764.description: Abstract . In this work, an extensive class of coherent states is introduced by taking the Fox–Wright function as the normalization function. It is demonstrated that these states satisfy the key requirements of continuity, normalizability and resolution of unity. Furthermore, coherent states associated with the continuous spectrum are obtained through a discrete-to-continuous limiting procedure.

pmc-10571791.title: The Cell-Autonomous Pro-Metastatic Activities of PD-L1 in Breast Cancer Are Regulated by N-Linked Glycosylation-Dependent Activation of STAT3 and STAT1
pmc-10571791.creator: Nofar Erlichman, Tsipi Meshel, Tamir Baram, Alaa Abu Raiya, Tamar Horvitz, Hagar Ben-Yaakov, Adit Ben-Baruch, Yona Keisari, Fabrizio Mattei, Anahid Jewett, Luyuan Li
pmc-10571791.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). PD-L1 has been characterized as an inhibitory immune checkpoint, leading to the suppression of potential anti-tumor immune activities in many cancer types. In view of the relatively limited efficacy of immune checkpoint blockades against PD-L1 in breast cancer, our recent study addressed the possibility that in addition to its immune-inhibitory functions, PD-L1 promotes the pro-metastatic potential of the cancer cells themselves.

pmc-10590750.title: Identification of key genes affecting sperm motility in chicken based on whole-transcriptome sequencing
pmc-10590750.creator: Shihao Guo, Yizheng Liu, Yaxi Xu, Kai Gai, Bailin Cong, Kai Xing, Xiaolong Qi, Xiangguo Wang, Longfei Xiao, Cheng Long, Yong Guo, Li Chen, Xihui Sheng
pmc-10590750.description: Sperm motility is an important index for the evaluation of semen quality. Improving sperm motility is important to improve reproductive performance, promote breeding process, and reduce production cost. However, the molecular mechanisms regulating sperm motility in chickens remain unclear. In this study, histological observation and whole-transcriptome analysis were performed on testicular tissue of chickens with high and low sperm motility.

pmc-11292701.title: Extensor Retinaculum Syndrome of the Ankle: An Adult Case Series
pmc-11292701.creator: Bradley Carlson, DuWayne Carlson, Tadiwanashe Chirongoma, D Kevin Scheid
pmc-11292701.description: Background:Extensor retinaculum syndrome (ERS) is a relatively rarely diagnosed compartment syndrome-like entity caused by elevated pressures in the tissues deep to the superior extensor retinaculum (SER). ERS is identified as out-of-proportion anterior ankle pain, pain with passive toe plantarflexion, elevated SER pressures (>40 mm Hg), and ultimately toe extension weakness and first web space numbness.

pmc-11420625.title: Liver transplant recipients have worse metabolic body phenotype compared with matched non‐transplant controls
pmc-11420625.creator: Chandra Bhati, Danielle Kirkman, Mikael F Forsgren, Hiba Kamal, Hiba Khan, Sherry Boyett, Olof Dahlqvist Leinhard, Jennifer Linge, Vaishali Patel, Samarth Patel, Susan Wolver, Mohammad S Siddiqui
pmc-11420625.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and AimQuantification of body compartments, particularly the interaction between adipose tissue and skeletal muscle, is emerging as novel a biomarker of metabolic health. The present study evaluated the impact of liver transplant (LT) on body compartments.MethodsTotally 66 adult LT recipients were enrolled in whom body compartments including visceral adipose tissue (VAT), abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (ASAT), muscle fat infiltration (MFI), fat‐free muscle volume (FFMV), and liver fat (LF) were quantified via whole body magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

pmc-11610721.title: A Review of the Clinical Presentation, Causes, and Diagnostic Evaluation of Increased Intracranial Pressure in the Emergency Department
pmc-11610721.creator: Cristiana Olaru, Sam Langberg, Nicole Streiff McCoin
pmc-11610721.description: Increased intracranial pressure (ICP) is encountered in numerous traumatic and non-traumatic medical situations, and it requires immediate recognition and attention. Clinically, ICP typically presents with a headache that is most severe in the morning, aggravated by Valsalva-like maneuvers, and associated with nausea or vomiting.

pmc-11639654.title: Double Sampling for Informatively Missing Data in Electronic Health Record‐Based Comparative Effectiveness Research
pmc-11639654.creator: Alexander W. Levis, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Rui Wang, Heidi Fischer, Sebastien Haneuse
pmc-11639654.description: Missing data arise in most applied settings and are ubiquitous in electronic health records (EHR). When data are missing not at random (MNAR) with respect to measured covariates, sensitivity analyses are often considered. These solutions, however, are often unsatisfying in that they are not guaranteed to yield actionable conclusions.

pmc-11709957.title: Usefulness of the Visual Cognitive Assessment Test in Detecting Vascular MCI in a Southeast Asian Cohort
pmc-11709957.creator: Pricilia Tanoto, Hannah En Ye, Ashwati Vipin, Yi Jin Leow, Faith Phemie Hui En Lee, Smriti Ghildiyal, Shan Yao Liew, Isabelle Yu Zhen Tan, Wayne Freeman Chong, Eunice Limin Seah, Mohammed Adnan Azam, Gurveen Kaur Sandhu, Fatin Zahra Zailan, Farid Tan Bin Hasyim Tan, Nagaendran Kandiah
pmc-11709957.description: BackgroundVisual Cognitive Assessment Test(VCAT) is a visual‐based cognitive evaluation tool which can be administered to multilingual populations without translation. VCAT has shown to be effective in differentiating mild cognitive impairment(MCI) from cognitively normal and useful for diagnosing MCI and mild AD(Kandiah et al., 2016).

pmc-12390596.title: Influence of Anthropometric Characteristics and Muscle Performance on Punch Impact
pmc-12390596.creator: Manuel Pinto, João Crisóstomo, Christopher Kirk, Javier Abián-Vicén, Luís Monteiro, Silvio Lorenzetti
pmc-12390596.description: Despite the known relevance of punch impact in boxing, limited evidence exists regarding how anthropometric and muscle performance variables contribute to it. This study investigated the relationship between anthropometric characteristics, muscle power and strength performance, and punch impact power in 69 boxing practitioners (mean ± SD age: 27.0 ± 6.1 years).

pmc-12559214.title: Selection and transmission of the gut microbiome alone can shift mammalian behavior
pmc-12559214.creator: Taichi A. Suzuki, Akbuğa-Schön Tanja, Jillian L. Waters, Dennis Jakob, Dai Long Vu, Mallory A. Ballinger, Sara C. Di Rienzi, Hao Chang, Ivan E. de Araujo, Alexander V. Tyakht, Ruth E. Ley
pmc-12559214.description: Animals live in partnership with their gut microbiota, and these microbial communities often shift when hosts adapt to new environments. While it is well known that the microbiome can influence traits ranging from metabolism to behavior, a key question remains unresolved: can host traits under natural selection be transmitted solely through the microbiome, without changes to the host genome?

pmc-12583510.title: Orphan nuclear receptor 4A1 (NR4A1) and NR4A2 are endogenous regulators of CD71 and their ligands induce ferroptosis in breast cancer
pmc-12583510.creator: Arafat Rahman Oany, Srijana Upadhyay, Wai Ning Tiffany Tsui, Amanuel Hailemariam, Sarah Latka, John D. Landua, Sandra D. Scherer, Alana L. Welm, Hugo Villanueva, Michael T. Lewis, Stephen Safe
pmc-12583510.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent cell death pathway that involves multiple genes, including the transferrin receptor (TFRC/CD71), glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and cystine-glutamate antiporter (SLC7A11). This study is based on the hypothesis that orphan nuclear receptor 4A1 (NR4A1) and NR4A2 maintain low levels of ferroptosis in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells and bis-indole derived (CDIM) compounds act as NR4A1/2 ligands that induce ferroptosis by enhancing CD71 expression.

pmc-13185038.title: Evaluation of AI tool assisting primary healthcare physicians to diagnostic and treatment tasks
pmc-13185038.creator: Tianran Wang, Jinyu He, Yiran Wang, Ning Zhang, Kaiyuan Chen, Wannian Liang
pmc-13185038.description: Primary healthcare (PHC) plays an important role in the healthcare system, yet the shortage of qualified primary healthcare physician (PHP) restricts the quality of diagnostic and treatment services provided by PHC institutions. The rapid development and prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI) offer a solution to this challenge.

pmc-13202395.title: Exploring home care nurses’ perceived competence and self-efficacy in palliative care delivery: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13202395.creator: Joanne Ta, Joanne Tay, Kathryn Pfaff
pmc-13202395.description: BackgroundIntegration of home-based palliative care (PC) enables patients to receive care at home, fosters family involvement, and reduces healthcare costs. Despite its benefits, nurses report challenges in delivering competent PC, and limited research has explored how home care nurses perceive their own competence and self-efficacy within this context.

pmc-13221396.title: Can Behavioral Interventions Promote Health Equity in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes? A Narrative Review of Promising Treatments
pmc-13221396.creator: Paul T Enlow, Jaquelin Flores Garcia, Julia Price, Kristen A Torres, David V Wagner
pmc-13221396.description: Purpose of ReviewSynthesize data on whether existing behavioral interventions can improve health equity among youth with type 1 diabetes.Recent FindingsWhile existing behavioral interventions demonstrated efficacy in improving health and/or psychosocial outcomes, evidence that these same interventions may improve health equity were lacking.

pmc-13354535.title: Fungal mucopyocele of the sphenoid sinus revealed by oculomotor and abducens nerve palsy: a case report
pmc-13354535.creator: Mohammed Chehbouni, Salah-Eddine Youbi, Omar Oulghoul, Youssef Lakhdar, Othmane Benhoummad, Youssef Rochdi, Abdelaziz Raji
pmc-13354535.description: Mucoceles of the sphenoid sinus are very rare accounting for 1% of all paranasal sinus mucoceles. Clinical symptoms are non-specific, extremely variable, and only occur when the mucocele impinges on surrounding structures. Secondary infection of a mucocele content is called mucopyocele and often result in rapid enlargement and acute onset of symptoms.
